title: Revelation
definition: Revelation is God's act of making Himself, His will, His truth, and His redemptive purpose known to humanity. God reveals Himself generally through creation and conscience, and specially through His Word and ultimately through Jesus Christ.
summary: The doctrine of revelation teaches that God is not silent. He has made Himself known so that people may know Him, worship Him, trust Him, and walk in His truth. General revelation shows God's power and glory through creation, but special revelation gives the saving knowledge of God through Scripture and through Jesus Christ. Because God has revealed Himself, faith is not built on human imagination but on the truth God has graciously made known.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the fullest and final revelation of God. In Him, the Word became flesh, the character of the Father is displayed, and God's redemptive purpose is made known. All true doctrine must lead us to behold Christ, trust Christ, and follow Christ.

studySections.heading: General Revelation
studySections.content: General revelation refers to what God has made known through creation, conscience, and His providential rule over the world. It reveals that God exists, that He is powerful, wise, and worthy of worship, but it does not by itself provide the saving message of the Gospel.

studySections.heading: Special Revelation
studySections.content: Special revelation refers to God's direct communication of truth through His words and acts, especially through Scripture and supremely through Jesus Christ. Through special revelation, God makes known His plan of redemption and calls sinners to faith, repentance, and life in Christ.

studySections.heading: Why Revelation Matters
studySections.content: Without revelation, humanity would be left to speculation. Because God has spoken, believers can know His truth, test every teaching by Scripture, and grow in a real relationship with Him through Christ by the power of the Holy Spirit.
